title: Walmart: From American dream to American NIGHTMARE
tags: get ready with me and makeup
description:
Hi friends, happy Wednesday! 

Do you guys remember that movie “Where the Heart Is?” It’s all about this girl who secretly moves into the store without anyone noticing, then she gives birth in the mattress department… and again, no one notices… It stars Natalie Portman, it’s great. 

When I was a kid and I saw this movie, it was 100% believable to me. I mean when I think of Walmart, I think of this ridiculously *HUGE* store with everything you could possibly need. 

I’m talking late night tampon runs, trashbags, nail polish removers, hot Cheetos and cream cheese… if you know you know. I honestly don’t even remember a time in my life when Walmart didn’t exist. 

Millions of Americans depend on their low prices just to get by in this economy. Walmart is a savior to some people. 

Others believe it’s the reason millions of Americans are in debt. I know… plot twist. Whatever you believe… Walmart is the biggest company in the world and *everyone* has an opinion on it. 

So of course I had to get the tea for us. Welcome to the Dark History of WALMART!

I appreciate you for coming by, and tune in next week for more Dark History.

But then everything started to go downhill….. they (very high management) started stretching us thin with responsibilities that we did not have enough people to do properly. They started giving people  less hours so they would do ALMOST the amount of time to get benefits but not quite. The company started hiring more people (more often than not with no experience) and paid them more than the rest of us who had been there for a few years. 
People started dropping like flies and I’m glad I got out when I did 🙃

Prescription glasses were invented in Northern Italy, likely Pisa or Venice, around 1268–1300. These early spectacles featured convex lenses to correct farsightedness, held together by a hinge to rest on the nose, primarily used by monks and scholars. 

Key milestones in the development of corrective eyewear include:

13th Century (c. 1284): First wearable eyeglasses, often attributed to Italian inventor Salvino D’Armate.

14th Century: Widespread use of eyeglasses (mostly reading stones/convex lenses) across Europe.

17th Century: Development of concave lenses to treat nearsightedness.

1727: Invention of temple glasses, allowing them to rest on ears.

1784: Bifocal lenses invented by Benjamin Franklin. 

Early spectacles lacked temples and required the user to hold them or balance them on the nose. The industry saw rapid growth after the 1440 invention of the printing press increased the demand for reading aids.
